QF.id: VII Introduction to Securities Broking Operations_53

question.text: Brokers should have Business Continuity Plan (BCP) / Disaster Recovery (DR) procedures that:

answer.text: Enable the broker to meet obligations during an emergency or significant business disruption and minimize business continuity incidents
Only store backup data without operational capability
Function only during annual testing exercises
Be located in the same building as the primary site

explanation.text: The Logic: Brokers must have BCP/DR procedures that enable them to meet obligations during an emergency or significant business disruption and to minimize business continuity incidents. The workbook supports BCP/DR setup and policy for continuity. The Trap: Backup-only storage with no operational capability, drill-only activation, or co-location with the primary site do not meet the regulatory expectation that the broker can continue to meet obligations during a disruption. Note: Specific DR-site takeover, geographic-separation, recovery-time-objective, and drill-frequency claims are not stated in the workbook pages checked (110-113); only the broader BCP/DR continuity expectation on page 110 is retained here.
